Kyushu to Tokyo

Eighteen nights, opening in a sleeping pod at Tokyo airport and closing on a flight home. Only three of them have a steering wheel in them. Pick a leg above.

Where you sleep

Eighteen nights across five stops. Two are settled: the airport pods and the Kyushu house. From Osaka on, three bedrooms where the price justifies it, two otherwise.

Night 0 · 16 Nov Tokyo airport Booked Sleeping pods at the airport, already booked. Land on the 16th, then the morning flight to Fukuoka.
Night 1 · 17 Nov Kurokawa Onsen — DeepSpot Booked 3 bedrooms, private sauna, 10 min drive from the village. €222 for four.
Night 2 · 18 Nov Takachiho One bed left in town Hold Guest House Iwato today — €75, free cancellation, nothing up front — then hunt Jalan and Rakuten for two proper rooms.
Night 3 · 19 Nov Miyazaki Options found City or coast, and the coast wins on driving: Aoshima is 1 h 52 m from the airport against Miyazaki's 2 h 01 m, with three-bedroom houses from €94. Miyazaki city keeps the nightlife.

Still open

Which Tokyo airport, on both the 16th and the 17th?

The pods pin down where you wake up on the 17th. The question is whether the Fukuoka flight leaves from that same airport. If the pods are at Narita and the flight goes from Haneda, that is a cross-city transfer of roughly two hours and the first trains do not run early enough for a 09:00 arrival in Fukuoka. Same airport for both and the start is simple.

What time does the car go back?

The airport is settled. The time is what decides whether the 20th is a drive or a wait: 10:00 leaves seven hours in the terminal, early afternoon buys Kirishima Jingu and possibly Ebino. Worth asking for while the booking is being redone.

Two nights still unbooked

Takachiho on the 18th needs a phone call — the only thing bookable online in the town itself is Guest House Iwato, and that is one room for four. Miyazaki on the 19th is a click away whenever you want it.

The 2026 Kumamoto earthquake

A magnitude 7.1 quake hit Kumamoto Prefecture on 28 July 2026, reaching shindo 7 — the top of the Japanese scale. Kurokawa, Nabegataki, Aso, Kikuchi and Kumamoto itself are all inside that prefecture, so most of the Kyushu leg sits in the affected area. What is known: Kumamoto Castle reopened in mid-August with new stone-wall damage, and Kikuchi Gorge was closed and has since had its entry ban lifted. Every route on this page plots normally, which suggests the main roads are open. But mountain sites here have been opening and closing, so check each one close to the date via the Japan Tourism Agency and JNTO status pages — and keep the free-cancellation bookings free-cancellation.

Book these before you fly

All online-only, all sell out. Two have cut-offs that fall before you land, and one has already mostly gone.

A bed in Takachiho — 18 Nov almost gone

Booking shows one property left in Takachiho for your night. A control search on a normal midweek date shows six, so this is peak-foliage scarcity, not thin coverage. Guest House Iwato is the last one — €75 for four, free cancellation, nothing to pay up front, so hold it today. Then hunt Jalan, Rakuten Travel or direct, where the ryokan actually sell. Airbnb has nothing whole-house in town; its best offer is Cottage-Blue in Gokase, 2 bedrooms for €137, 14 km out.

Takachiho Gorge rental boat — 19 Nov opens 5 Nov · shuts 17 Nov 09:00

The window opens exactly two weeks ahead and closes 9:00 AM two days before your slot. Online only — no phone, no time-slot requests, no waitlist. Same-day tickets are sold at the gorge reception in the morning only. Operating hours are decided each morning around 8:00 on water level and weather.

Nabegataki Falls — 14:00 or 15:00 on the 17th refundable until 14 Nov

Advance online booking only, in timed slots. ¥300 an adult, 9:00–17:00 with last entry 16:30, capped at 40 minutes to an hour with no re-entry. Book it for arrival day rather than the 18th — that swap is what makes the crater fit.

Night 2: Takachiho

Takachiho is booked out for the 18th across every channel. What is left needs a phone call.

18 Nov, across three channels genuinely booked out

Ryokan Association grid: of 24 properties, 13 explicitly full, 1 open, 1 nearly gone, 9 publish nothing. Jalan, for Hotel Takachiho (39 rooms): 18 Nov marked × — as is every date from the 17th to the 29th. Booking.com: 1 of 6. Peak foliage has taken the town.

Why the list stops at 19 km

Booking has nine more between 20.8 and 23.8 km, around Takamori and Minamiaso. What they cost, measured as the whole of day 19 — base to the gorge, gorge to Miyazaki:

BaseDay 19 drivingPenaltyBack after the 20:00 kagura
Takachiho, in town1 h 57 m—minutes
Gokase, 14–17 km2 h 12 m+15 mabout 20 min
Mamihara, 18.6 km2 h 20 m+23 mabout 25 min
Takamori, 21–24 km2 h 40 m+43 m43 min
A second night in Kurokawa3 h 16 m+1 h 19 mtoo far — no kagura

So the 20 km cluster is out. Not because it is far in kilometres, but because 43 minutes of mountain road each way around a 20:00 kagura means somebody is not drinking and everybody is up late, and it adds 43 minutes to the next day as well.

And a second night in Kurokawa is not the same thing. It is 1 h 19 m from the gorge rather than Takamori's 43, and far enough that the kagura simply does not happen — which is the reason for being in Takachiho at all. Gokase stays the sensible fallback at +15 minutes.

Night 3: the city or the coast

The 19th ends wherever you choose, and the choice changes both days. Sleeping in Miyazaki means driving down the coast and back up again; sleeping on the coast means you are already there.

BaseDay 20 to the airportDay 19The trade
Aoshima1 h 52 marrive, coast on the doorstepa seaside village, no nightlife
Miyazaki city2 h 01 mcoast is an out-and-backNishitachi, food and bars
Nichinan, by Udo2 h 12 mleast total driving of the threefurthest from the airport

Aoshima is quicker to the airport than Miyazaki, not slower. It sits south of the city and the airport run heads inland south-west, so you start partly on the way. That was worth measuring rather than assuming — the intuition points the other way.

Aoshima gets the vote. Quickest to the airport of the three, the Devil's Washboard and the island shrine are a walk rather than a scheduled stop, and a three-bedroom house starts at €94 — which makes the room split a non-decision. What you give up is Nishitachi: Aoshima is a small seaside village, so if the group wants a proper night out, Miyazaki city is the one.

The route, day by day

17Tue

Land at Fukuoka, drive south to the onsen

Sleep · DeepSpot — booked

  • Morning flight from Tokyo, landing 09:00 · car at 10:00After a night in the airport pods. Fukuoka to Kurokawa is only 1 h 45 m direct, so the afternoon is genuinely yours rather than a transfer.
  • Mameda-machi, Hita — lunchA preserved Edo merchant street of white-walled townhouses, sitting directly on the route. An hour is enough.
  • Nabegataki Falls — pre-booked slotA wide, low curtain of water you walk behind.
  • Kurokawa Onsen village — eveningBuy the tegata pass, around ¥1,500 for three baths. The village is at its best after dark in a yukata.
1 h 45 m · 114 km Fukuoka Airport → Kurokawa, direct
1 h 59 m via Hita and Nabegataki — the stops cost 14 minutes
18Wed

Over the caldera rim to Takachiho

Sleep · Takachiho

  • Daikanbo & the Milk Road — from about 09:40The northern rim of the Aso caldera, looking down the whole crater floor.
  • Nakadake crater & Kusasenri — around 11:30November gate hours 8:30–17:00. Access is cancelled on the morning if volcanic gas is high, so check at breakfast before committing the drive.
  • Amano-Iwato & Amanoyasugawara — 15:00, in daylightThe cave where the sun goddess hid, and a river cave filled with thousands of stacked stone cairns.
  • Takachiho Yokagura — 20:00, Takachiho ShrineAn Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property, danced nightly, about an hour. The same myth you stood in that afternoon.
2 h 27 m · 113 km Kurokawa → Daikanbo → Kusasenri → Takachiho

Leave DeepSpot by 09:00 and this day has slack in it. Sunset is about 17:20, and with Nabegataki done on arrival day the crater and the Amano-Iwato shrines both fit before dark.

19Thu

The gorge, then down to the coast

Sleep · Miyazaki

  • Takachiho Gorge by boat — at openingYou row yourself to the foot of the 17-metre Manai Falls. First slot means the best light and the thinnest crowd.
  • Aoshima ShrineAn island shrine ringed by the Devil's Washboard, a shelf of wave-cut rock ribs exposed at low tide.
  • Udo JinguA vermilion shrine built inside a sea cave in the cliff face. The most striking single thing on this coast.
  • Nishitachi, MiyazakiThe nightlife quarter. Chicken nanban was invented in this prefecture — eat it here, with the local beef.
1 h 57 m · 134 km Takachiho → Miyazaki, tolls
1 h 13 m · 58 km Miyazaki → Aoshima → Udo → Obi, whole coast run
20Fri

The inland run to the airport

Car back at the airport · flight 17:00 · Osaka 20–24

  • Sekinoo Falls, MiyakonojoPotholes among the largest in the world, a National Natural Monument since 1928, with suspension bridges over the gorge. Free entry and parking. Budget 30 minutes for the falls alone, 50 with the potholes, 60 for the full loop. Food outlets can be shut midweek, and the 20th is a Friday.
  • Kirishima JinguA shrine in deep cedar forest on the volcano's flank, twenty minutes from the airport. Around 45 minutes to an hour.
  • Kareigawa StationOpened 1903, the oldest wooden station building in Kyushu and a National Registered Cultural Property since 2006 — original waiting room and ticket counter still in place. Ten minutes from the airport, so it is the natural last stop. Fifteen minutes is enough.
  • Ebino Highlands, only with a late returnCrater lakes on the rim above Kirishima and real autumn colour, but a winding climb that adds nearly an hour.
1 h 34 m · 122 km Miyazaki → Kagoshima Airport, nothing on the way
2 h 01 m all three stops — twenty-seven minutes more driving

A workable shape, if the car goes back at 14:00. Leave Miyazaki 08:30 · Sekinoo Falls 09:40 to 10:30 · Kirishima Jingu 11:20 to 12:10 · Kareigawa Station 12:45 to 13:00 · airport 13:10. Three real stops and still an hour of slack before the return.

At a 10:00 return none of it fits — you would leave Miyazaki at 08:15, drive straight through, and wait seven hours for the flight. This is the argument for asking.

Day 17: the long way

Everything competes for one deadline — Nabegataki's last entry at 16:30. With the car at 10:00 that is six and a half hours to spend, and each option eats into it. Measured:

Shape of the dayDrivingCostFits?
Hita → Nabegataki (planned)1 h 59 m—lots of slack
Dazaifu → Kurume → Nabegataki2 h 47 m+48 myes, comfortably
Kumamoto → Nabegataki3 h 17 m+1 h 18 myes, an hour spare
Dazaifu → Kumamoto → Nabegataki3 h 38 m+1 h 39 m20 min of margin
Dazaifu → Kurume → Kumamoto → Nabegataki4 h 01 m+2 h 02 mno — misses the gate

The suggestion: skip Kumamoto, take Dazaifu and Kurume. Car at 10:00, Dazaifu 10:30 to 11:45, Kurume for lunch 12:20 to 13:15, Nabegataki 14:45 to 15:45, DeepSpot by about 16:05 — in good time for the village baths. Two stops that are properly memorable, and still an easy day after a night in an airport.

Kumamoto costs 30 minutes more than both of those together and what you get is a castle mid-reconstruction: it reopened in August 2026 after the earthquake with new stone-wall damage, and the rebuild runs to 2052. Worth it if a great castle is the point; not worth it as a stop on the way somewhere.

And if you want Kikuchi Gorge — 11 minutes of driving but an hour of walking — the only honest way is to move Nabegataki to the 18th and drop the Nakadake crater. That is a real trade, not an addition.

What is actually worth stopping for

  • Dazaifu Tenmangu — 30 min from the airportOne of the country's principal shrines, in wooded grounds. The draw for a first day is the approach: around thirty shops grilling umegae mochi to order — red bean paste inside, pressed on a hot iron stamped with a plum blossom, crisp outside and chewy within. Eat it walking, straight off the griddle.
  • Kurume — lunch, on the expresswayTonkotsu ramen was invented here, at a stall called Nankin Senryo, in 1937. The milky white broth everyone now knows came ten years later and by accident, when a cook at a shop called Sankyu left the pot on too long and boiled the bones to emulsion. Eating it in the town that invented it is a better story than most museums.
  • Kumamoto Castle — the +1 h 18 m optionOne of Japan's three great castles, seen mid-repair. Sakuranobaba Josaien at its foot is the easy lunch; Suizenji Jojuen, an Edo strolling garden built as a miniature Tokaido complete with a small Mount Fuji, is 30 minutes away.
  • Kikuchi Gorge — only with the tradeFour kilometres of clear water and moss under broadleaf forest, one of Kumamoto's best autumn walks, and mid-November is the week. Closed after the quake, entry ban since lifted.

If you add more days

Everything on the map's could add layer, grouped by where the extra night actually goes. Nothing here needs the route redrawn.

A night at the front, before KurokawaThe Oita onsen belt

  • Yufuin — smart, walkable onsen town with a lake and a long craft street. Sits almost exactly on the Fukuoka–Kurokawa line, so it costs you nothing in distance.
  • Beppu — the big one: steam vents across a whole hillside and eight distinct hot-spring fields. Roughly an hour east of Kurokawa.

A night in the middle, around AsoCaldera and castle

  • Takamori & Minamiaso — the caldera's southern floor, and the moss-covered cave shrine at Kamishikimi Kumano Imasu. This is also where the spare beds are, as the map shows.
  • Kumamoto Castle — one of Japan's three great castles, about an hour west of Aso. A detour rather than a stop, so it wants its own half-day.
  • Gokase — not a sight, but 14 km from Takachiho and the closest place with rooms if the town stays full.

A night at the end, before KagoshimaKirishima and the bay

  • Kirishima Jingu, Sekinoo Falls, Kareigawa Station — all three are built into day 20 now, not add-ons. Together they cost 27 minutes of extra driving.
  • Ebino Highlands — crater lakes and autumn colour above Kirishima, but a winding climb: it adds nearly an hour to the airport run, so it needs a late car return.
  • Sakurajima — a live volcano directly across the bay from Kagoshima, reached by a ferry that runs through the night.

Or stretch the coast dayFurther down Nichinan

  • Cape Toi — wild horses grazing on an open headland at the southern end of the Nichinan coast, below Obi.
  • Nobeoka — the coastal gateway, if you would rather reach the sea on the 18th than the 19th.
